source_text:
Ἐγὼ γὰρ καὶ μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτὸν οἶδα καὶ πιστεύω ὄντα.
καὶ ὅτε πρὸς τοὺς περὶ Πέτρον ἦλθεν, ἔφη αὐτοῖς: Λάβετε, ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ δαιμόνιον ἀσώματον. καὶ εὐθὺς αὐτοῦ ἥψαντο καὶ ἐπίστευσαν, κραθέντες τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι. διὰ τοῦτο καὶ θανάτου κατεφρόνησαν, ηὑρέθησαν δὲ ὑπὲρ θάνατον.
μετὰ δὲ τὴν ἀνάστασιν συνέφαγεν αὐτοῖς καὶ συνέπιεν ὡς σαρκικός, καίπερ πνευματικῶς ἡνωμένος τῷ πατρί.
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Smyrna, refuting those who say Christ only seemed to suffer, and here he gives his own testimony about the risen Christ.
pass_a_gloss: I for also after the resurrection in flesh him I know and I believe being. And when to those around Peter he came, he said to them: Take, touch me and see, that not I am a demon bodiless. And immediately him they touched and they believed, having been mixed with the flesh of him and with the spirit. Because of this also death they despised, and they were found above death. After but the resurrection he ate with them and he drank with them as fleshly, although spiritually united to the Father.

choices.term: ἐν σαρκὶ αὐτὸν οἶδα καὶ πιστεύω ὄντα
choices.english: I know and believe that he was in the flesh
choices.why: The participle ὄντα with ἐν σαρκί is a periphrastic construction; rendering it as 'that he was in the flesh' preserves the indirect statement while keeping the flesh language from the glossary.
rejected: I know him to be in the flesh
I know and believe him being in flesh

choices.english: Take hold of me, touch me and see
choices.why: Λάβετε is an imperative meaning 'take' or 'take hold of'; adding 'of me' makes the command clear in English while keeping the direct address.

choices.term: κραθέντες τῇ σαρκὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ πνεύματι
choices.english: being joined to his flesh and his spirit
choices.why: κραθέντες literally means 'having been mixed/blended'; 'joined to' conveys the intimate union without the physical mixing image that could mislead.
rejected: having been mixed with his flesh and spirit
blended with his flesh and spirit

choices.why: The adjective σαρκικός is used substantivally; 'as one who is fleshly' preserves the adjectival force and the contrast with 'spiritually united'.

choices.english: even though he was spiritually united to the Father
choices.why: καίπερ with a participle is concessive; 'even though' captures the contrast between his fleshly eating and his spiritual union with the Father.
rejected: although spiritually united to the Father
though being spiritually united to the Father

bible_refs.note: ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ δαιμόνιον ἀσώματον

pass_b_english: For I know and believe that he was in the flesh even after the resurrection.

And when he came to those around Peter, he said to them: "Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon." And immediately they touched him and believed, being joined to his flesh and his spirit. For this reason they also despised death, and they proved to be beyond death.
After the resurrection he ate and drank with them as one who is fleshly, even though he was spiritually united to the Father.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'flesh' for σάρξ, but 'bodiless' is fine. However, 'Take hold' misses the sense of 'handle/touch' for ψηλαφήσατέ; more critically, the glossary term 'flesh' is not used where σαρκικός appears.
last_rejected.fix: "Handle me, touch me and see" and "as one who is fleshly" → "as flesh"
last_rejected.ruling: Λάβετε means 'take/hold'; ψηλαφήσατε is rendered 'touch'. No meaning lost; glossary complaint is unclear and unsupported.

last_rejected.why: The brief marks this as Jesus Christ speaking, but the English uses 'he' without identifying the speaker as Jesus, potentially confusing readers.
last_rejected.ruling: ἔφη αὐτοῖς is correctly 'he said to them'; pronoun 'he' refers to αὐτόν (Christ) from prior sentence. No error.

polish.changed: Clarified that Jesus' words mean he is not a bodiless spirit or demon, and preserved the paradox that he remained fleshly after the resurrection while spiritually united to the Father.

notes.quote: he was spiritually united to the Father
notes.why: After resurrection, 'spiritually united' seems to deny bodily resurrection.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'united in spirit with the Father' or 'spiritually, [he was] with the Father.'

notes.quote: Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon
notes.why: Jesus says 'not a bodiless demon' but means 'not bodiless, not a demon'; awkward double negative.
notes.fix: Note: 'Greek may mean 'not bodiless, [that is], not a demon.'

notes.quote: Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon
notes.why: Loose conflation of Luke 24:39 ('a spirit has not flesh and bones') with different wording.

polish.changed: Removed the incorrect Scripture reference, clarified that Jesus is the speaker, and kept the quotation intact without adding a comparison that the source does not make.

notes.why: Unexplained reference to post-resurrection appearance; not standard 'disciples' or 'apostles'.
notes.fix: Note this refers to Luke 24:34 or similar resurrection appearance.

notes.why: The quote does not match Luke 24:39 exactly; Luke says 'a spirit does not have flesh and bones.'
notes.fix: Note that this is a loose paraphrase of Luke 24:39.

polish.changed: Clarified that Jesus is the speaker in the second paragraph by naming him explicitly, and kept the quotation as a summary rather than a Scripture citation.

notes.quote: Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon
notes.why: Scripture-like words but not identified; actually a summary, not exact quote.

notes.quote: Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon
notes.why: Paraphrase of Luke 24:39 and John 20:27, not exact citation; no book named.
notes.fix: Identify as paraphrase of Luke 24:39 / John 20:27.

problems.quote: he said to them: "Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon."
problems.why: Quoted as Jesus's words but introduced with 'he said to them' after 'he was in the flesh'; reader may need clearer 'Jesus said'.

problems.quote: "Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon."
problems.why: Cited as words of Jesus but closest to Luke 24:39 ('touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones'); 'bodiless demon' is Ignatius's elaboration, not direct quotation.
problems.fix: Add note: 'Ignatius's paraphrase of Luke 24:39, adapted against docetism.'

edits.old: he said to them: "Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon."
edits.new: Jesus said to them: "Take hold of me, touch me and see that I am not a bodiless demon."

fixed: Clarified 'he said' to 'Jesus said' since the speaker is Jesus Christ, as marked in the work brief voices.

No edit made for the scripture note: the English accurately renders the source's 'Take, touch me and see, that not I am a demon bodiless,' and the work brief does not require adding a note about Luke 24:39.
